title: Debt and Contact
premise: Lena Reyes, a freelance interpreter who built her career on being unattributable, receives a calendar invitation from Marcus Hale—her former handler, dead for six months—for a meeting at a Geneva hotel bar. The meeting is real: a defector named Ilse Brandt carries proof that the peace delegation Lena serves was engineered to fail, and someone inside Lena's own agency sold the operation. As Lena smuggles Ilse toward a dawn extraction flight, she discovers the invitation was bait set by the mole to flush out whoever Hale trusted most. In the end, Lena chooses love over duty—burning her cover to save Ilse, exposing the mole with Hale's dead-man's-switch cache, and walking away from the profession that made her invisible.
about_author: Sable Crane is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working high-security diplomatic summits across Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose words are worth more than their lives.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Six months after handler Marcus Hale's funeral, Lena interprets a fractious ceasefire session in Geneva and goes home to find a calendar invite from his account: tomorrow, 9 p.m., Hotel Cornavin bar. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread—the dead don't send meetings.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV Lena. She verifies the invite through old tradecraft channels; it's authentic, or a flawless forgery. Her current handler, Voss, warns her off anything connected to Hale, calling him compromised. Beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: POV Lena. At the Cornavin, no ghost appears—but a woman slips her a phone: Ilse Brandt, mid-level analyst defecting with files proving the peace delegation was sabotaged from inside. Beat: the trap has teeth, but so does the prize.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carries
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Flashback chapter: how Ilse found the sabotage evidence and why she trusts only Hale's network—which leads to Lena. Beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The phone contains Hale's contingency cache, half-locked, addressed to 'the one I didn't burn.' Lena realizes Hale anticipated his death and chose her as failsafe. Beat: reluctant inheritance of a dead man's war.

chapters.title: The Delegation Fails on Schedule
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The ceasefire talks collapse exactly as the leaked files predicted; Lena, interpreting the failure in real time, recognizes phrases planted by an insider. Beat: horror of watching a script performed live.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Voss orders Lena debriefed and confined after the collapse; she plays compliant while copying the cache. A small kindness from him rings false. Beat: paranoia becomes method.

chapters.title: Half a Key
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The cache needs a second key Hale gave to someone else. Clues point to his estranged daughter, Nadia, in Lyon. Beat: the personal cost of a spy's double life.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In Lyon, Nadia hates her father's memory and refuses until Lena shows her the invitation—he planned for family even in death. She surrenders the key but begs Lena not to open what's inside. Beat: love against duty, mirrored.

chapters.title: The Mole's Shape
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Unlocked, the cache names three candidates for the mole—including Voss—and reveals the extraction flight is already known to the enemy. Beat: every ally now suspect.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse makes contact with Lena directly, mistrustful, testing her with details only Hale would know. They agree to move tonight. Beat: two strangers betting their lives on each other.

chapters.title: Housekeeping
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena discovers her apartment searched, her own file flagged 'attributable'—someone is erasing her invisibility deliberately. Beat: the price of survival is becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Long Way Out
chapters.summary: POV both, alternating. Lena extracts Ilse from a safehouse under surveillance, using interpreter misdirection to walk them past a checkpoint. Beat: competence as intimacy; trust begins.

chapters.title: Confessions at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Hiding in a freight depot, Lena and Ilse trade truths—Hale was like a father to Lena; Ilse betrayed her country for a conscience. Beat: love kindling where duty should be.

chapters.title: Flight Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The extraction flight leaves at dawn from a private strip near Annecy; the cache says the enemy knows. Lena must decide whether the flight itself is bait. Beat: dread of the obvious trap.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Voss intercepts her, offering protection if she delivers Ilse to him alone—revealing he knows too much to be innocent, yet too little to be the mole. Beat: the middle player, pitiable and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Re-reading the cache, Lena realizes the third candidate—delegation chair Ambassador Kessler—is the mole, and the flight intel came from him. Beat: the failure had a face all along.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse admits she may have been allowed to defect—a lure to expose Hale's network. Choosing to go anyway, she hands Lena the files as insurance. Beat: courage as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Annecy
chapters.summary: POV Lena. At the airstrip, Kessler's team springs the trap; Lena springboards Hale's dead-man's-switch—broadcasting the sabotage files publicly—turning exposure into armor. Beat: climax; the invisible woman speaks loudly.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Lena. With the plane burning on the tarmac, Lena and Ilse escape overland, Lena burning her covers and credentials to do it. Beat: sacrifice of identity for love.

chapters.title: Kessler Falls
chapters.summary: POV multiple, brief. The broadcast forces arrests; Voss, half-redeemed, closes the net on Kessler. Nadia learns her father died protecting something true. Beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Attributable
chapters.summary: POV Lena, epilogue. Months later, Lena and Ilse live quietly under new names; a fresh meeting invitation arrives—from Sable Crane. Lena smiles, deletes it, and chooses the morning in front of her. Beat: survival finally priced right.
